newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo spill seen easier to clear than Jan disaster.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo spill seen easier to clear than Jan disaster.

text.p: The light crude oil spilled from the supertanker Diamond Grace in Tokyo bay on Wednesday in Japan's biggest oil spill ever is likely to be easier to handle than the heavy fuel oil dumped from a Russian tanker last January, experts said.

Although the estimated 13,400 tonnes of light crude spilled from the Japanese-owned Diamond Grace was volatile, bay winds had dissipated the oil and virtually eliminated the danger of fire, Kyodo news agency quoted the Maritime Disaster Prevention Centre as saying.
The oil, which Gulf traders said was predominantly Umm Shaif from Abu Dhabi, could largely be recovered using pumps, the centre said.
That the accident occurred during summer with relatively mild winds, clear weather and calm seas was also likely to aid operations.
By contrast, the 5,200 tonnes of heavy fuel oil leaked by the Russian tanker Nakhodka when it broke in two in the Sea of Japan was too thick, and January seas were too choppy, to operate pumps.

Clean-up workers instead used small fishnets and buckets to scoop up the heavy crude amid choppy seas and winter winds that scattered globs of oil across more than 500 km (300 miles) of scenic coastline and rich fishing grounds.
